newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom warned of picket by 22,000.
newsitem.headline: Telekom warned of picket by 22,000.

text.p: Some 22,000 members of the National Union of Telecommunications Employees (NUTE) threatened to picket Telekom Malaysia Bhd if it does not allot staff five percent of shares soon, the Bernama news agency said on Monday.
Union president Mohamed Shafie Mammal said NUTE was dissatisfied with the apparent reluctance of Telekom's board to allocate the shares, approved by the government 14 months ago.
Shafie told reporters that Telekom's board had informed NUTE that it would give out the shares, estimated at 160 million units, by end of this year at the lowest market price for the week.
Telekom officials could not be immediately reached for comment.
Shafie said the union feared Telekom's share price would "spiral" the longer the share distribution took. At the end of last week, Telekom's shares were traded at 23.40 ringgit ($9.36).
On Monday, Telekom shares ended down 30 cents to 23.10.
He said NUTE's executive committee members had decided to meet on Thursday to discuss follow-up action against Telekom, including holding pickets, Bernama said.
